chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the two said: Regarding

a man who has a debt due at a specified term, and his creditor comes to him and says, 'Pay me such and such amount from what is owed to me, and I will forgive the remainder for you,' or he says, 'Pay me part of it, and I will extend the term for what remains.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I see no harm in that, provided he does not add anything to the principal amount.'
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'For you is the principal of your debts; you do no injustice, nor are you treated unjustly.'

key_terms.لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ: you do no injustice, nor are you treated unjustly

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to forgive part of a debt and extend the time for the rest?
ai.summary: Reported by prominent Shia scholars including Al-Baqir and Al-Sadiq, this hadith validates debt restructuring through partial forgiveness or term extension, provided the total repayment does not exceed the original principal to avoid riba (usury). It underscores the Shia legal principle of fairness in financial transactions, linking the practical resolution of debt to the Quranic injunction against injustice in Surah Al-Baqarah.
